title: Troubleshooting Trap Siphonage and Vent Blockages
description: When a fixture gurgles or drains slowly while another fixture is running, negative pressure inside the drainage system is often pulling water out of the P-trap. Proper drain ventilation introduces atmospheric air to break this vacuum and protect the liquid trap seal. If vent pipes are blocked by debris, bird nests, or frost, air cannot flow freely, resulting in siphoned traps and sewer gas entering the building. Troubleshooting involves inspecting roof vent terminals, checking air admittance valves where installed, and clearing obstructions to restore proper atmospheric pressure balance throughout the system.

Troubleshooting Trap Siphonage and Vent Blockages

When a fixture gurgles or drains slowly while another fixture is running, negative pressure inside the drainage system is often pulling water out of the P-trap. Proper drain ventilation introduces atmospheric air to break this vacuum and protect the liquid trap seal. If vent pipes are blocked by debris, bird nests, or frost, air cannot flow freely, resulting in siphoned traps and sewer gas entering the building. Troubleshooting involves inspecting roof vent terminals, checking air admittance valves where installed, and clearing obstructions to restore proper atmospheric pressure balance throughout the system.
